title: Check yourself: Artifacts, skills, research and plugins

questions.stem: A consultant must hand a client a one-page dashboard that the client will open, adjust and forward. The consultant also wants to try a different layout without losing the first one. Which approach fits?

options.text: An inline reply, with each layout pasted into a fresh chat and compared by eye
options.says: Ruled out because an artifact opens in a panel "so you can edit and re-use it without scrolling back through a conversation".

options.text: A skill, with each layout saved as its own custom skill in the account
options.says: Ruled out because a skill is "A repeatable procedure used across many chats", not a deliverable the client can open.

options.text: An artifact, with the alternative started by editing an earlier message
options.says: An artifact opens in its own panel for editing and sharing, and editing an earlier message branches the chat so "each branch has its own artifact".

options.text: A Research run, with each layout requested as a new report with citations
options.says: Ruled out because Research is for "An open question that needs many sources and citations", and this task has known content to lay out.

origin.section: Artifacts: a deliverable beside the conversation

questions.stem: A finance team builds its monthly report inside a Project called Finance. A manager who works in separate chats outside that Project needs the same house layout. Which feature carries that procedure to both places?

options.text: Written rules in the Finance Project's own instructions
options.says: Ruled out because "Project instructions apply to every chat in that Project", and the manager's chats sit elsewhere.

options.text: A plugin installed for the whole department
options.says: Ruled out because a plugin is "A role's bundle of procedures and connections", far more than one layout.

options.text: An artifact kept as the pattern for each new report
options.says: Ruled out because an artifact is "A document, deck, dashboard or small tool to hand to someone" and does not make later chats follow a layout.

options.text: A custom skill that Claude loads when the task matches
options.says: A skill is a reusable procedure that Claude pulls in "in any chat where it is enabled", inside or outside a Project.

origin.section: Skills: a playbook Claude loads when it is relevant

questions.stem: A colleague shares a ZIP file of a "free time-saving skill" from an unknown site and asks you to upload it. What is the best response?

options.text: Upload it straight away and watch the first few replies for anything odd
options.says: Ruled out because "from an unknown source it is a route for prompt injection", and odd behaviour may never show in a reply.

options.text: Decline the archive and ask for a copy from a source you already trust
options.says: Skills carry instructions and scripts that Claude follows, so the page says to install skills only from trusted sources and to review what they bundle.

options.text: Upload it for yourself only and keep every colleague away from it
options.says: Ruled out because the risks named, "prompt injection and data exfiltration", apply to the person who installs the skill, not only to colleagues.

options.text: Upload it to a test chat and judge it by the first reply it gives
options.says: Ruled out because the first reply cannot show hidden scripts or instructions, which is why the page says to review "code dependencies and bundled resources" first.
